item.title: Jetten warns of rising hate at WorldPride conference
item.description:
Jetten warns of rising hate at WorldPride conference

August 5, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Prime minister Rob Jetten has warned that hatred and intolerance against the LGBTQI+ community are growing, and that “hard-won progress” on equal rights is eroding around the world. He was speaking at the WorldPride Human Rights Conference in Amsterdam.

He said that many countries are backsliding on equal rights legislation and that homophobic hate speech is becoming more overt and aggressive. This is fuelled, he said, by “toxic, highly organised and well-funded groups hiding behind the façade of freedom of expression.”

He also referred to the Islamist attack at Berlin’s pride event on July 25, in which one person was killed and 29 injured. The suspect was later shot dead by police.

Jetten said despite the anger and sorrow, his “heart was filled with hope” when thousands gathered at Amsterdam’s Homomonument, the memorial to LGBTQI+ victims of persecution, days later in commemoration.

The prime minister’s speech was interrupted immediately after he took the stage as pro-Palestinian demonstrators began chanting “where is your red line” – referring to the protests against the Gaza war last year. One shouted “shame on you being at a human rights conference when you’re complicit in genocide.”

He responded as the protesters were being escorted out by asking the audience to give them a round of applause and describing the situation in Gaza and the West Bank as “horrific.”

Online hatred rising

Homophobia is spreading so rapidly because big social media companies are “barely moderating content for hate speech,” Jetten said.

Hate groups “no longer feel restrained,” he continued, “in my view, the rise of online hatred is one of the biggest threats facing LGBTQI+ people today… Misinformation – and disinformation – can be spread in the blink of an eye, with a single mouse-click.”

“Reaching much further than NGOs, youth workers and health organisations can.
This is always how hatred takes hold: In the shadows. Outside the spotlight of society. Underestimated by everyone.”

Funding and education initiatives
Over the next three years the government will invest €7.5 million annually in improving the safety of the queer community, Jetten said, and that a public information campaign will be launched to combat discrimination and disinformation.

Some of the money will fund Purple Friday, the day on which Dutch schools devote special attention to diversity, with pupils and teachers wearing purple to show their support. It has been run since 2010 by the GSA network of LGBTQI+ rights organisation COC and now involves thousands of primary and secondary schools.

The day has also become a point of contention. Surveys by NOS and RTL in 2024 found three-quarters of participating schools had run into problems, from posters being torn down to rainbow flags being set alight, and some had dropped it or rebranded it as a general “be yourself” day.

The conference comes 25 years after the Netherlands became the first country in the world to open marriage to same-sex couples. Four couples married at Amsterdam city hall a minute after midnight on April 1, 2001, and some 36,000 same-sex couples have married since.

item.title: Glasshouses feel cost of drought as sprinkler ban imposed
item.description:
Glasshouses feel cost of drought as sprinkler ban imposed

August 5, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Glasshouse operators in the Westland region could lose tens of millions of euros after a ban on sprinklers comes into force on Wednesday.

The glasshouse industry has not been exempted from the ban, which has been imposed by the Delfland water authority as an anti-drought measure.

All sluice gates in the region have been closed to protect drinking water from being contaminated by saltwater from the sea. Inspectors will check if companies are complying with the ban on using water for sprinkling.

“These measures are urgently needed to prevent irreversible damage happening,” a spokesman for the water board told Omroep West. “The glasshouse owners have been given until midnight [on Tuesday] to fill their reservoirs.”

Glastuinbouw Nederland, which represents the industry, said a two to three-week ban would cost companies around €150 million.

It has asked the water board if companies can spray their crops with purified waste water or seawater. “Almost any water is better than no water,” a spokesman said.

A ban on drawing water is also in force in parts of the Brabantse Delta region, around Breda. The ban, which initially covered the hours from 9am to 9pm, was extended last week to 24 hours and include fruit growers, who were previously exempt.

On the island of Terschelling, off the coast of Friesland, sheep have been banned from grazing and inspections of dykes have been stepped up amid concerns that the drought is causing cracks to appear.

item.title: Two women die trying to help a child in the sea at Callantsoog
item.description:
Two women die trying to help a child in the sea at Callantsoog

August 5, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Two women died after going into the sea to help a child in trouble off Callantsoog in Noord-Holland on Tuesday afternoon.

A 39-year-old British woman, who had been missing overnight, was found dead on the beach at Groote Keeten, north of where the group ran into difficulty. A 26-year-old woman from Gelderland died on Tuesday after being pulled from the water and given CPR.

The two women went to the aid of a child who was at risk of drowning at about 4.30pm and then got into trouble themselves, broadcaster NOS reported. The child and another swimmer were brought ashore by the lifeguard service and taken to hospital for checks.

The alarm was raised at the Voordijk beach entrance, between Callantsoog and Groote Keeten. Four KNRM lifeboat stations took part in the search alongside the lifeguard service, the coastguard and police, using boats and helicopters from surrounding areas.

The search was called off shortly after 9pm on Tuesday because of the tide and resumed on Wednesday morning.

Police are not investigating the circumstances further, regional broadcaster NH reported. Neither woman has been named.

item.title: Belgium and Netherlands open new high-voltage power line
item.description:
Belgium and Netherlands open new high-voltage power line

August 5, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Netherlands and Belgium have opened a new high-voltage power line that will allow 30% more electricity to flow between the two countries.

The so-called Brabo III project connects Antwerp’s harbour to the Rilland high-voltage station across the border in Zeeland. The scheme is designed to reduce strain on the electricity grid and reduce electricity prices in both countries.

Dutch prime minister Rob Jetten and his Belgian counterpart Bart de Wever both attended the official opening in Antwerp. Jetten said the link was an important step towards ensuring European countries can produce their own energy.

“In recent years that has rapidly become a security issue,” he said. “It might not be how the Brabo III project started, but in today’s world it is an important element.”

De Wever said the line, which will supply power to companies such as BASF and Ineos, was “a new artery for our industry”.

Belgian grid operator Elia has spent 10 years building the power line, including two 192 metre-high masts at the Kallosluis, which links the Schelde to the Waaslandkanaal.

The Netherlands will be able to export up to 30% more solar and wind energy on high production days, while at other times it can import more power to meet rapidly increasing demand.

Utrecht has currently frozen all new applications for high-voltage electricity connections because the network has reached saturation point, while operator Tennet warned earlier in the year that some areas were approaching maximum capacity.

item.title: Bomb disposal experts called in at Limburg wildfire
item.description:
Bomb disposal experts called in at Limburg wildfire

August 5, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The wildfire near Venray in northern Limburg is under control, but efforts to fight the blaze are being hampered by the presence of unexploded munitions in the ground in an area that experienced heavy fighting at the end of the Second World War, the Limburg-Noord safety authority told broadcaster NOS.

Something that may be an unexploded shell was spotted in the Boschhuizerbergen nature reserve on Tuesday and experts from the defence ministry’s bomb disposal unit were called in. Heavy fighting took place around Venray during the war.

Explosions have been heard in the area over the past two days, but a fire service spokesman told NOS it is not certain these came from munitions. Intense heat can turn resin and moisture inside trees to steam, bursting the wood with a bang.

Keeping crews back from the buried ordnance is not slowing the operation down, the safety authority said, because the heat in those parts of the reserve would be unbearable either way.

Days of work ahead
“The fire stayed stable overnight,” Erik Thijssen of the safety authority told NOS on Wednesday morning. “There was no further spread.” He said the all-clear had not been given but the situation was “stable and manageable”.

Thijssen said putting the fire out completely would take several more days.
An emergency ordinance issued by the mayor of Venray on Tuesday afternoon remains in force. It bars people from entering the area and from flying drones over it.

Helicopters and crews
Defence ministry Chinook helicopters are due back in the air between 10am and 11am, the local safety authority told regional broadcaster L1 Nieuws.

The helicopters had dropped almost 900,000 litres of water on the fire by Tuesday evening, drawn from the Maas in buckets holding 7,600 litres.

Around 100 hectares have burned. The fire is being held inside “stop lines” – a railway line, an asphalt road and wide forest tracks – and firefighters are being rotated in from North Brabant, Utrecht, Drenthe and Friesland.

item.title: Fourth teenager arrested in anti-terrorism investigation
item.description:
Fourth teenager arrested in anti-terrorism investigation

August 5, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A fourth teenager has been arrested by police investigating a suspected terror plot, the Dutch prosecution service has said.

The 18-year-old was arrested at his home in Kesteren, Gelderland, on Friday evening by a police special intervention team (DSI) acting on information from the intelligence agency AIVD.

A magistrate in Rotterdam ordered him to be detained in custody for the next 14 days. His contact is restricted with his lawyer.

No weapons were found at his home and prosecutors said there were no signs an attack was imminent.

“At this point in the investigation we have not identified a clear target or moment for an attack,” the prosecution service (Openbare Ministerie) said in a statement.

Last week three youths aged 16, 17 and 19 were arrested in overnight raids at homes in Rotterdam, Alkmaar and Eindhoven.

The eldest suspect, named as Mohammed K., was convicted two years ago of planning attacks on nightclubs and police stations in Belgium, none of which took place.

The other two were among a group of 14 people aged between 14 and 30 who were arrested last April on suspicion of inciting terrorism via the social media platform TikTok.

item.title: Dutch man arrested for racing on German motorway at 235km/h
item.description:
Dutch man arrested for racing on German motorway at 235km/h

August 5, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A Dutch man has been arrested for driving his Porsche 911 at speeds of up to 235 km/h on a German motorway while allegedly under the influence of cannabis.

The section of the A3 near Koblenz where he was stopped has no speed limit, but the 23-year-old man was pulled over for “extremely dangerous” driving after he weaved in and out of traffic and tailgated a police car.

A drug test revealed traces of THC, the active ingredient in cannabis, in his system. The man told police he ran a coffeeshop in Eindhoven with his father and regularly took the drug “for professional reasons”.

Police said traffic was relatively heavy for the time of day when the man was stopped just after midday on Monday. “It was only through good fortune that there were no traffic accidents,” they said.

The man has been charged with racing on the highway and dangerous driving. Police confiscated his driving licence and ordered him to pay €10,000 in bail before being released.

He was collected from the police station in Montabaur, 25km west of Koblenz, by his father.

In a separate incident across the border, a man from Rotterdam was arrested after reaching speeds of 246 km/h on the A15 while under the influence of drink and drugs.

The 40-year-old was stopped after passing a speed check near Papendrecht on Tuesday night on a section of motorway where the limit is 100 km/h.

His car was impounded and his licence seized by police after he was charged with dangerous driving and driving under the influence.

item.title: Fast food outlets almost double in under 20 years
item.description:
Fast food outlets almost double in under 20 years

August 5, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Netherlands had 19,435 fast food outlets at the start of 2026, an increase of 88% since 2007, according to figures published on Wednesday by national statistics agency CBS.

The count covers cafeterias, sandwich shops, food stalls and ice cream parlours, which now make up slightly more than half of all the country’s 38,600 food outlets.

Restaurants grew more slowly over the same period, rising 73% from 11,055 to 19,165. Because fast food outlets expanded faster, they overtook restaurants in 2020 and have outnumbered them since.

Cities and the coast
Nearly 20% of all fast food outlets are in the four largest cities. Amsterdam has 1,605, Rotterdam 975, The Hague 790 and Utrecht 445.

Measured against population, however, the densest concentrations are not urban. The national average is close to 1.1 outlets per 1,000 residents, and it is tourist areas that push well beyond it.

Vlieland has 8.3 outlets per 1,000 residents, the highest in the country, followed by Schiermonnikoog on 4.1 and Terschelling on 3.1. Coastal municipalities in Zeeland, Zandvoort in Noord-Holland and Valkenburg aan de Geul in Zuid-Limburg also rank highly.

The east and northeast have fewer outlets per head than the national average. Staphorst in Overijssel has the fewest, at 0.3 per 1,000 residents, almost four times below the average.

item.title: NEC draw 0-0 at Olympiacos to boost Champions League hopes
item.description:
NEC draw 0-0 at Olympiacos to boost Champions League hopes

August 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

NEC Nijmegen kept their hopes of a place in the Champions League alive with a 0-0 draw against Olympiacos in Greece.

The match was an even contest, with both teams notching up 10 chances over the 90 minutes.

The home side dominated the early exchanges, but Dick Schreuder’s side were stronger in the second half as Cape Verdean midfielder Jamiro Monteiro and Noé Lebreton went close for NEC.

Monteiro, newly signed from PEC Zwolle, replaced Japanese midfielder Kodai Sano, who was left out of the team at his own request pending his expected move to PSV Eindhoven for €14.5 million.

Former Ajax forward Dusan Tadic came on in the second half to make his debut for NEC at the age of 37, replacing the 35-year-old Bryan Linssen in the front line alongside the 38-year-old captain Tjaronn Chery.

It was NEC’s first taste of European football since a team coached by Mario Been lost 1-0 to HSV Hamburg in the UEFA Cup in 2009.

The two teams will play the return leg in Nijmegen’s Goffertstadion next Tuesday, August 11, with the winners going through to a play-off against either Union Saint-Gilloise of Belgium or Norwegian side Bødo/Glimt for a place in the lucrative group stages.

item.title: Local mayors step up pressure to end border checks after crashes
item.description:
Local mayors step up pressure to end border checks after crashes

August 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The mayor of a border town has urged transport minister Vincent Karremans to hold talks with his German counterpart about border checkpoints following a string of serious accidents.

Four people have died in collisions near the border and at least 10 have suffered serious injuries since Germany reintroduced stricter checks in December 2024.

In the most recent incident last Friday, three people were injured in a crash involving four vehicles, including two lorries, on the A12 at Babberich, just before the border.

The German government has said it wants to extend the controls into the autumn, despite the implement of the European Migration Pact, which Dutch foreign minister David van Weel said would make the checkpoints “a thing of the past”.

Aad van Oosten, acting mayor of Zevenaar, urged Karremans to raise the issue with German interior minister Alexander Dobrint, who is a supporter of extending the controls.

“We have tried to raise awareness of our situation with other councils in the area, both in the Netherlands and Germany,” he told Omroep Gelderland. “All we get in reply is that there is no alternative.”

Chaos on roads

Van Oosten is not the first Dutch local politician to raise concerns about the impact of German border checks. In March Mark Boumans, mayor of Doetinchem, called for them to be scrapped following another five-vehicle collision, also at Babberich, in which three people were injured, including a child.

The following month Hubert Bruls, mayor of Nijmegen and chair of the council of Dutch regional safety boards, said the checks had cost millions of euros of damage and lost income and led to chaos on minor roads.

Bruls disputed the effectiveness of the checks after figures showed just under 3,500 people were suspected of trying to enter Germany illegally from the Netherlands and 1,750 were turned away at the border in six months.

Dutch officials checked the documents of 123,320 people at the border and turned 470 away in the first nine months after selected checks were introduced.

Van Oosten said the frequency of the accidents showed they could not be put down to inattentive motorists. “People should pay attention while driving, but this is a serious matter that is not as simple as just paying more attention,” he said.
